atlas-tw.0001: German companies in Taiwan look for bilingual staff who can at least communicate in English, but graduates’ English is often only passive; returning graduates from abroad form a bilingual pool in high demand.
atlas-tw.0002: TSMC’s 2026 campus recruitment took applications to 30 April with interviews to 30 June, and its summer internship (6 July to 28 August) took applications to 8 May; the National Taiwan University campus fair was held on 7 March 2026 with 347 companies and more than 40,000 positions.
atlas-tw.0003: TSMC planned to hire around 8,000 engineers and technicians in 2026, and 104 Job Bank listed 21,762 finance, accounting and tax openings in May 2026, up 6.0% on a year earlier.
atlas-tw.0004: Taiwan’s unemployment rate was 3.32% in August 2026 (seasonally adjusted) and 11.74% among 15- to 24-year-olds; 147,000 people entered the workforce in 2024, 5.3% fewer than in 2023, and 71.7% of them held a university degree and 19.5% a graduate degree.
atlas-tw.0005: Unusually open for graduates of its own universities: they can now stay up to two years after graduating and work in any job without a work permit. After that, a points test rewards pay and Chinese. Taipei is the finance capital: 35 of the 40 domestic banks have their head office there.
atlas-tw.0006: Taiwan’s banking and insurance headquarters city
atlas-tw.0009: 35 of 40 have their head office in Taipei
atlas-tw.0012: Taiwan was not covered by the research library before this record.
atlas-tw.0014: Of Taiwan’s 40 domestic banks, 35 have their head office in Taipei, and all 14 domestic property and casualty insurers are based there.
atlas-tw.0015: Taiwan’s first science park and its chip-making base
atlas-tw.0016: the chipmaker’s registered business address is in Hsinchu Science Park
atlas-tw.0017: TSMC’s filings with the US Securities and Exchange Commission give its business address as No. 8, Li-Hsin Road 6, Hsinchu Science Park, Hsinchu, Taiwan; its latest annual report on Form 20-F was filed on 16 April 2026.
atlas-tw.0018: Companies in the Hsinchu science parks
atlas-tw.0020: Central Taiwan’s science park for precision machinery and optoelectronics
atlas-tw.0021: Manufacturers in the Central Taiwan Science Park
atlas-tw.0023: The Hsinchu Science Park Bureau oversees six parks where over 600 companies have been approved to operate, employing more than 160,000 people, with average annual revenue above NT$1,000 billion in recent years.
atlas-tw.0024: The Central Taiwan Science Park, centred on Taichung, had sales of over NT$936 billion in 2020 and more than 51,827 employees at 219 manufacturers.
atlas-tw.0025: No family is rated in Hsinchu or Taichung: the science-park figures read give companies and staff, not hiring by role. Tainan and Kaohsiung are not mapped: the Southern Taiwan Science Park and Kaohsiung port statistics could not be read.
atlas-tw.0026: Apart from the central bank’s lists of banks and insurers, TSMC is the only employer named, from its US Securities and Exchange Commission filing; MediaTek’s head office could not be confirmed from a source we can cite. No family is rated in Hsinchu or Taichung, so their standing rests on the science parks’ own statistics.
atlas-tw.0027: Taiwan’s statistics office publishes no GDP by city or county that was found, so no hub has a GDP figure; wages are the 2024 average annual total pay of full-time Taiwanese employees by workplace city (Hsinchu County, which shares the science park, is separate), population is the usual resident population, and Hsinchu has no Numbeo rent.
atlas-tw.0028: Country brief: three hubs, pay and standing
atlas-tw.0029: The Global Financial Centres Index 40 (September 2026) ranks Taipei 42nd of the centres it lists (rating 717), up nine places from 51st.
atlas-tw.0030: In 2024 the average annual total pay of full-time Taiwanese employees, by workplace, was NT$1,298,000 in Hsinchu City, NT$1,003,000 in Hsinchu County, NT$947,000 in Taipei City and NT$673,000 in Taichung City, against NT$776,000 nationally; the median was NT$902,000 in Hsinchu City, NT$735,000 in Taipei and NT$517,000 in Taichung.
atlas-tw.0031: In 2024 new entrants to the workforce earned NT$37,000 a month on average (up 6.4%): NT$34,000 for university graduates and NT$52,000 for graduate-school graduates; the median was NT$33,000, and NT$49,000 for graduate school.
atlas-tw.0032: On 1 January 2026 Taichung had 3,076,000 usual residents, Taipei 2,441,000, Hsinchu County 675,000 and Hsinchu City 509,000; the country had 23.71 million.
atlas-tw.0033: Graduates of Taiwanese universities who later need a work permit can qualify with 70 points, scored on degree, pay, experience, Chinese and languages; the Ministry of Labor formally abolished annual numerical quotas on 1 August 2024.
atlas-tw.0034: Whether employers expect Mandarin for entry roles was not researched; immigration rules, fees and tax are consolidated in visas_immigration/taiwan/.
atlas-tw.0035: The two-year permit-free stay took full legal effect under the amended Foreign Professionals Act on 1 January 2026 (WDA circular 4 Feb 2026).
atlas-tw.0036: Taiwan’s largest employers recruit graduates on campus: TSMC holds job fairs at the main universities each year for students graduating that year, alongside summer internships for enrolled students, and the National Taiwan University fair of 7 March 2026 had 347 companies offering more than 40,000 positions. Most other hiring runs through local online portals, of which 104 Job Bank is the standard for specialists.
atlas-tw.0037: Campus recruitment drives and career fairs
atlas-tw.0038: TSMC’s campus drive is open to bachelor’s, master’s and PhD students graduating in 2026 or able to start by the end of the year; applications ran to 30 April and interviews to 30 June. It also plans visits to National Taiwan Normal University and Taipei Tech.
atlas-tw.0039: The National Taiwan University “VISION 2026” campus fair on 7 March 2026 had 347 companies at 450 booths and more than 40,000 positions, a record for the university; 70% of the companies offered cross-disciplinary roles. EY was there, recruiting 2026 graduates for audit, tax, financial accounting advisory and technology risk.
atlas-tw.0041: Financial groups recruit through management-associate (MA) programmes on campus fairs in March. In the 2017 season Fubon was taking about 30 recruits, CTBC more than 50, First Bank about 60 reserve officers and E.SUN 500 hires plus 30 MA and TMA places; SinoPac required TOEIC 750 and First Bank TOEIC 900. Those figures are from 2017.
atlas-tw.0042: Pay in the programmes was quoted as reaching or exceeding NT$1 million a year for the best-paid tracks (Cathay, Fubon, China Life), not guaranteed for every MA role.
atlas-tw.0043: Summer internship that turns into an offer
atlas-tw.0044: TSMC’s summer internship ran from 6 July to 28 August 2026, with applications to 8 May and interviews to 29 May; it requires enrolment, accepts undergraduates from the third year and prefers master’s and PhD students, and strong interns may receive full-time offers.
atlas-tw.0045: A Taiwanese-degree graduate can also take an internship after graduating by extending the residence permit for that purpose; the NTU career centre handles eligibility.
atlas-tw.0047: Local online portals are the main recruiting channel: 104 Job Bank is the standard for specialists and managers, with 1111 Job Bank, 518 Job Bank and Yes123 as other local boards, LinkedIn growing for international roles, and Cake.me and Yourator posting in several languages. 104 listed 21,762 finance, accounting and tax openings in May 2026, up 6.0% on a year earlier.
atlas-tw.0048: Companies often use the messaging app LINE to arrange interviews and make first contact.
atlas-tw.0049: Work first on the job-seeking stay (Taiwanese-degree graduates)
atlas-tw.0050: A graduate of a Taiwanese university can extend the residence permit for up to two years to look for work and may work freely in that time without a work permit, full-time or part-time (Workforce Development Agency circular of 4 February 2026). This is how foreign graduates start in jobs and internships that would otherwise need a permit.
atlas-tw.0051: Experienced hires: portals, LinkedIn and the Employment Gold Card
atlas-tw.0052: Experienced foreign professionals can use LinkedIn and the Talent Taiwan portal; the Employment Gold Card is a 4-in-1 permit that allows a change of job or freelance work without employer sponsorship. German companies in Taiwan look for bilingual staff, and returning graduates from abroad are a bilingual pool in high demand.
atlas-tw.0053: The overall unemployment rate was 3.32% in August 2026 (seasonally adjusted), but 11.74% among 15- to 24-year-olds. TSMC planned to hire around 8,000 engineers and technicians in 2026.
atlas-tw.0054: Competition for accounting graduates is pushing pay up: in May 2026 the Big Four raised audit-department pay by about 9% (PwC), at least 10% (Deloitte) and about 12% (EY and KPMG) on average.
atlas-tw.0055: New entrants to the workforce numbered 147,000 in 2024, down 5.3% on 2023.
atlas-tw.0056: Taiwanese financial groups recruit on campus through management-associate (MA) programmes; the Anue report on the 2017 season names Cathay, Fubon, CTBC, Shin Kong, Yuanta, SinoPac, China Life, E.SUN, First Bank and KGI Bank among the firms at the campus fairs.
atlas-tw.0057: The Big Four compete hard for audit graduates: in May 2026 they raised audit pay by about 9% to 12% on average, KPMG and EY raised new-graduate starting pay by NT$2,000, Deloitte by 5% and PwC by an unspecified amount. KPMG said high performers could reach NT$1 million a year within two to three years.
